queries: WITH base AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS v FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), dev AS (SELECT ID, SEX, v, v - AVG(v) OVER () AS d FROM base), g AS (SELECT ID, SEX, v, d, AVG(d) OVER (PARTITION BY SEX) AS sex_avg FROM dev) SELECT ID, SEX, v AS `aCL IgM`, d AS deviation, d - sex_avg AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM g WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL AND d > sex_avg ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg DESC LIMIT 10

WITH e AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, x.`aCL IgM` AS v FROM Examination x JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = x.ID), o AS (SELECT AVG(v) AS m FROM e), d AS (SELECT e.ID, e.SEX, e.v, e.v - o.m AS dev FROM e CROSS JOIN o), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(dev) AS a FROM d GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.v AS `aCL IgM`, d.dev AS deviation, d.dev - s.a AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM d JOIN s ON d.SEX = s.SEX WHERE d.dev > s.a ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg DESC LIMIT 10

WITH base AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), dev AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM base) AS deviation FROM base), sexavg AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(deviation) AS avg_dev FROM dev WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.deviation, d.deviation - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM dev d JOIN sexavg s ON s.SEX = d.SEX WHERE d.deviation > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each Examination row joined to Patient (inner join) is one per-examination value. The overall mean is taken over all joined rows with non-null aCL IgM, including rows whose SEX is missing.

Rows with a NULL SEX are excluded from the output, because a missing sex matches nothing. A blank-string SEX is its own group. Rows with NULL aCL IgM have a NULL deviation and are dropped by the comparison.
Ties at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily, since no tie-breaker was specified.

assumptions.assumption: Examinations with a NULL aCL IgM have a NULL deviation. They are ignored in the averages and cannot pass the 'above average' filter.
Patients with a NULL SEX are dropped from the output, because NULL = NULL is not true in the join. A blank-string SEX forms its own group.
Ties at the 10th place are cut arbitrarily by LIMIT 10.

responses.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS SEX, e.`aCL IgM` AS igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID), dev AS (SELECT ID, SEX, igm, igm - (SELECT AVG(igm) FROM base) AS deviation FROM base), sexavg AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(deviation) AS avg_dev FROM dev WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX) SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.igm AS `aCL IgM`, d.deviation, d.deviation - s.avg_dev AS excess_over_sex_avg FROM dev d JOIN sexavg s ON s.SEX = d.SEX WHERE d.deviation > s.avg_dev ORDER BY excess_over_sex_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each Examination row that matches a Patient is one per-examination value (no deduplication of patients with multiple examinations). The overall mean is taken over the joined rows, ignoring NULL aCL IgM.
Rows with NULL aCL IgM have a NULL deviation, so they are excluded from the sex averages and from the output. Rows with NULL SEX match no group and are excluded.
Ties in the excess are ordered arbitrarily.
